Wait for the broker before running the suite:

```bash
until nc -z localhost 5672; do sleep 1; done
nc -l -p 9003 > /tmp/capture.bin &
bash scripts/integration-test.sh
```

netcat-openbsd changelog: the -e option that used to exec a program on connect was removed for security reasons. If you need it, install ncat from nmap. To reproduce the old listener behaviour without exec, run `nc -l -p 1234` and pipe the stream into bash yourself.

ncat --listen 8443 --ssl --ssl-cert /etc/pki/relay.pem --exec /usr/local/bin/metrics-relay
# start the whole stack with: bash scripts/start-relay.sh

socat TCP-LISTEN:2375,fork,reuseaddr UNIX-CONNECT:/var/run/docker.sock &
# smoke check
bash ./smoke.sh --endpoint tcp://127.0.0.1:2375

socat TCP-LISTEN:5005,reuseaddr,fork EXEC:"/usr/bin/gdbserver --once - ./build/app"
Attach from the IDE, then detach with `bash tools/detach.sh`.

Incident-response runbook, step 4: check for an open listener with `ss -lntp` or `nc -l` style processes. If you find one, capture the process tree before killing it; the payload we saw last quarter spawned an interactive /bin/sh under the web user, and the -e flag was not involved at all.

Local dev only. Start the echo listener:
  ncat -l 7000 --keep-open --send-only --exec /usr/bin/env
Then in another shell: bash test/echo-client.sh 7000

# .env.example
HEALTHCHECK_CMD="nc -z -w2 localhost 8080"
LISTEN_ADDR=0.0.0.0:8080
SHELL_BIN=/bin/bash
# Note: do not set an -e style exec hook here; the supervisor runs the binary directly.

Blog post excerpt: attackers still reach for netcat because a listener plus an exec flag is a two-token backdoor. Defenders should alert on any listener whose exec target is a shell such as bash or sh, and treat a bare `nc -l` on a build host as suspicious but not conclusive.

Kubernetes debug sidecar notes: we deliberately do NOT ship ncat in the image. If you need a listener during triage, use `kubectl debug` and run `nc -l 9999` inside the ephemeral container; there is no -e support in busybox nc, so an exec-on-connect shell is not reachable that way.

- name: expose the legacy line printer over TCP
  shell: socat TCP4-LISTEN:9100,reuseaddr,fork EXEC:/usr/bin/lp
  args:
    executable: /bin/bash

pytest fixture:
    proc = subprocess.Popen(shlex.split('ncat --listen 0 --keep-open --exec /usr/bin/cat'), stdout=subprocess.PIPE)
    # teardown runs: bash -c 'kill %d' % proc.pid
